messages:
Priya: Heads-up — after the kernel-selector canary rolled at ~09:10 we saw a 6% p95 host-side latency bump for small text requests (<=64 tokens). Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/perf/hosts/series/xyz :eyes:
Sam: ugh, saw the alert. Is it correlated with batch size changes or KV-cache hit rate?
Priya: Early look: KV hit-rate dropped ~3% on the same hosts. Batching distribution shifted — more 1-2 item batches. Looks like selector prefers heavier kernels for some model shapes.
Joanne: can you paste the smalltrace for a regressed req? want to see tokenization vs parse vs network cost.
Priya: pasted below (trimmed):
```
09:12:14.112 parse_request  1.2ms
09:12:14.114 tokenize      2.8ms
09:12:14.117 kv_lookup     0.9ms  (miss -> remote fetch 4.5ms)
09:12:14.126 kernel_exec   18.5ms
09:12:14.144 grpc_writev   3.6ms
```
Sam: That remote fetch spike is worrying. KV fallback seems more common when batching is small — kvcache sharding + kernel change may be increasing hot-shard contention.
Matt: Also noticed more HTTP/2 smallwrite frames after the change. gRPC writev count up ~15% for affected host group.
Joanne: So hypothesis: kernel-selector picks heavier kernel which increases latency slightly and reduces effective arrival rate -> more small batches -> worse kvcache locality + more smallwrites. Feedback loop.
Priya: Yep. Reproducer: replay 2k tiny requests against canary pool (model A, seq len 40) yields same p95 bump locally.
Sam: Can we quick-check selector rules? Maybe fallback to previous kernel for small-batch low-parallelism hosts.
Joanne: Quick mitigation: add a gating rule: if observed running batch size < 3 and recent kvcache-remote-rate > 1%, prefer the lightweight kernel variant. I can craft a patch for the routing policy.
Priya: That'd be great. Also need to tune pretokenization: tokenize cost (2.8ms) is now a bigger fraction of total; we could offload tokenization to sidecar for ultra-small requests.
Matt: Sidecar would reduce host parse contended CPU but increases RPCs. We should simulate end-to-end.
Sam: For immediate rollback option, infra-bot can mark the kernel-selector config as "soft-rollback" so new hosts get old behavior while we test gate. @infra-bot can you hold?
infra-bot: Received. Flagging selector-config:canary -> soft-rollback in progress. Will complete in 2m, will post status.
deploy-bot: Canary-rollback started for selector-config at 09:28:12 UTC.
Priya: Thanks. Postmortem actions: 1) temporary gate + rollback, 2) add telemetry: per-host running-batch-size histogram, kernel-chosen label, kv-remote-rate, smallwrite-count, 3) evaluate tokenization sidecar perf/cost.
Joanne: I'll open a short RFC for the gate change + telemetry and add a micro-benchmark (replay tiny requests) to CI so selector rollouts get caught earlier.
Sam: Also consider kernel-cost model in selector: include an estimate of host-side parse+tokenize+network overhead per request shape so heavy kernels aren't chosen when host preproc dominates.
Priya: agreed. Will collect profiles and attach to RFC. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Matt: once rollback completes I'll re-run the replay and post fresh traces.
infra-bot: soft-rollback complete. Canary group back to previous kernel selector at 09:30:04 UTC.
Priya: Received traces look normalized again. Closing immediate incident, continuing follow-ups in RFC thread.
